rules.rule: Never introduce, log, commit, echo, serialize, or expose credentials, API keys, access tokens, private keys, cookies, service-role secrets, or production environment values. Secret placeholders and variable names are allowed; real secret values are not.

Changes to authentication, authorization, admin routes, service-to-service trust, JWT/OAuth handling, or permission checks must preserve fail-closed behavior and must not weaken an existing access-control boundary without explicit security justification and tests.

Database migrations must be additive or explicitly safe, preserve production data, avoid destructive or irreversible operations without a documented rollback/repair path, and must not bypass the repository's governed preview/apply process.

Do not bypass, weaken, remove, or silently short-circuit protected production approvals, environment gates, CodeQL/security checks, dependency checks, deployment verification, or required CI status checks.

Changes to public or cross-service API contracts must preserve backward compatibility unless the pull request explicitly documents a breaking change and updates all known callers, validation, and tests.

MoneyHub, trading, liquidity, billing, payment, or accounting changes must not execute irreversible financial actions by default. Require explicit authorization boundaries, idempotency where applicable, auditability, and safe failure behavior.

Agent-orchestrated actions that mutate production systems, external services, user data, deployments, or infrastructure must have an explicit authorization boundary and must not silently escalate from read-only analysis to mutation.

Material behavior changes should include or update focused tests. Flag changes that alter business logic, security behavior, API contracts, migration behavior, or orchestration without a credible validation path.
